## v0.30.0 - 2026.10.29

This is the stable release of vLLM Ascend v0.30.0, built on the v0.29 release line and aligned with upstream vLLM v0.30.0 via the main2main pipeline. Building on v0.30.0rc1, this release integrates FlashMLA decode with DCP and DSpark, extends KV Pool layerwise pooling and PCP speculative decoding, hardens EPLB for the new quantization formats, and fixes the stability issues across attention, MoE, KV transfer, and Model Runner V2 execution reported during the RC cycle. It still focuses on the flagship models: DeepSeek V4.1, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSeek V4-Flash/Pro, Kimi K3.   * Qwen3.8-27B: Supported non-contiguous KV cache in hybrid linear-attention models, respected per-layer KV cache dtype and kept KV cache contiguous for paged attention, restored C8 V scales on hybrid cache page reassignment, restored Mamba block tables before deferred PP postprocessing, added the FLA NPU backend for GDN prefill, and fixed 310P performance and kernel compatibility for quantized deployment. #14340 #17924 #18003 #17956 #17954 #17565 #17534 #16420 #17964 #17278†
  * Kimi K3 on Ascend: Added end-to-end Kimi K3 support, including MLA DSpark speculative decoding, no-RoPE MLAPO on Ascend 950, fused QKV projections, fused norm gate and attention residual, EPLB, MegaMoE, and projector rotation. #12950 #13277 #13507 #13989 #13509 #14231†
  * GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 / DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 accuracy and performance: Resolved GLM-5.2 DSpark acceptance regressions and DeepSeek V4 Flash-0731 / Pro-0813 accuracy issues (reasoning-effort alignment, routed SwiGLU limit, and frontend behavior), and reused DSV4 compressor metadata across layers for better performance. #10697
  * Added experimental Gemma4 support on A2 and Ascend 950. #11091 #10643
  * Improved the DeepSeek V4 prefix-cache hit rate. #11107

### Performance

  * Optimized SFA DSA-CP output merge with All-to-All communication and PCP FlashAttention restore/output merge. #12137 #11842
  * Avoided H2D synchronization in context-parallel speculative decoding metadata and snapshotted query locations before asynchronous H2D copies. #11862 #12071
  * Parallelized KV-cache receive with a thread pool and enabled asynchronous all-gather for DSA-CP output-projection TP weights. #10548 #10694
  * Vectorized local sequence-length computation in SFA metadata. #11816

### Stability and Bug Fixes

  * Fixed GLM-5.1 IndexCache weight loading and a GLM-4.7-Flash `IndexError` on the first request with MTP and layerwise MemCache. #11363 #11829
  * Fixed Qwen3.5 GDN accuracy regressions across PCP, MTP, and DCP graph replay, including a mixed-length PCP out-of-bounds crash, while restoring the previous model-runner dispatch behavior. #11195 #11893 #12027 #12283
  * Fixed Qwen3.5 speculative-decoding accuracy, garbled output, and out-of-bounds failures on Ascend 310P with MTP/EAGLE and full-graph execution. #11337 #11408 #11920
  * Fixed Qwen MoE routing overflow and shared-expert gate matrix-multiplication failures on Ascend 310P. #11391 #11730
  * Fixed Qwen3-Omni ModelSlim W8A8 checkpoint loading failures caused by mismatched weight names and unquantized embedding metadata. #12321
  * Fixed Qwen3-VL rotary-embedding copy races on Ascend 310P and restored the device-specific VisionTransformer patch. #11679 #12132
  * Fixed the DeepSeek-R1-0528 W8A8 shared-expert no-clamp accuracy path without regressing the clamped DeepSeek V4 path. #11775
  * Fixed DeepSeek V4 Flash W4A8-MXFP4 all-gather EP inference on Ascend 950 by preserving routing-weight precision. #11498 #11663 #11718
  * Fixed malformed streamed tool-call arguments and TP8+EP startup compatibility for MiniMax-M2 and MiniMax-M2.5. #11505
  * Fixed silent prefix-cache output corruption and block-table overflow for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, and other hybrid Mamba models using MTP/EAGLE, plus a 310P Mamba align-postprocess hang. #11353 #11659 #12038
  * Fixed Mooncake KV-transfer grouping for Kimi-K2.7 Code with Kimi-K2.5-DFlash when P/D nodes use unequal TP sizes and target/draft models have different global KV-head counts. #11887
  * Fixed the AscendStore parent-block hash chain when a KV block group is only partially missing. #12252
  * Disabled shared-expert multistream overlap when fused MC2 is enabled to avoid an unsupported configuration. #12245
  * Fixed DCP/DP service hangs and restricted the recompute scheduler to decode nodes. #12034 #11490
  * Delayed AscendStore initialization until the first real decode request. #11673
  * Fixed low MTP acceptance rates for SFA with DSA-CP and multiple speculative tokens. #10878

### 7. How does vllm-ascend work with vLLM?

`vllm-ascend` is a hardware plugin for vLLM. Stable releases usually align with the same vLLM version, while RC releases may use the corresponding vLLM final release version. For example, `vllm-ascend` `v0.18.0rc1` matches vLLM `v0.18.0`. For the main branch, we ensure that `vllm-ascend` and `vllm` are compatible at every commit.

### 8. Does vllm-ascend support Prefill-Decode (PD) Disaggregation feature?

Yes, vllm-ascend supports Prefill-Decode Disaggregation feature with Mooncake backend. See the official tutorial for example.

### 9. Does vllm-ascend support quantization method?

Currently, w8a8, w4a8, and w4a4 quantization methods are already supported by vllm-ascend.

### 10. How is vllm-ascend tested?

vllm-ascend is tested in three aspects: functions, performance, and accuracy.

  * Functional test: We added CI, including part of vllm's native unit tests and vllm-ascend's own unit tests. In vllm-ascend's tests, we test basic functionalities, popular model availability, and supported features through E2E test.

  * Performance test: We provide benchmark tools for E2E performance benchmark, which can be easily re-run locally. We will publish a perf website to show the performance test results for each pull request.

  * Accuracy test: We are working on adding accuracy test to the CI as well.

  * Nightly test: we'll run full test every night to make sure the code is working.

For each release, we'll publish the performance test and accuracy test report in the future.

### 11. How to fix the error "InvalidVersion" when using vllm-ascend?

The problem is usually caused by the installation of a development or editable version of the vLLM package. In this case, we provide the environment variable `VLLM_VERSION` to let users specify the version of vLLM package to use. Please set the environment variable `VLLM_VERSION` to the version of the vLLM package you have installed. The format of `VLLM_VERSION` should be `X.Y.Z`.

## Description

drslark

opened on Sep 14, 2026

Issue body actions

### Your current environment

Environment used during investigation
    
    `vLLM Ascend main
    Ascend 950DT
    GLM-5.2 W4A4C8
    PD deployment with SFA/DSpark
    TP/DP configurations used during validation included TP4/DP2 and TP8/DP1
    FULL_DECODE_ONLY compiled execution
    `

The exact `collect_env.py` output is not available from the affected remote deployment anymore. The issue has been reduced to CPU-mock regression tests for the three incorrect runtime assumptions below.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Background

This issue was found while validating GLM-5.2 DSpark speculative decoding on Ascend A5 (950DT). The affected setup uses the SFA/DSpark path on current `main`, including PD serving and compiled `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` execution. The three problems below were isolated from the same A5 GLM DSpark accuracy investigation, although each is an independent runtime-correctness issue.

GLM-5.2 SFA/DSpark serving on current `main` can produce incorrect output or enter an invalid execution path because several decisions that vary by runtime batch are derived from initialization/profile state or are traced outside an opaque compiled boundary.

The investigation found three independently reproducible correctness problems.

#### 1. SFA PROLOG_V3 can incorrectly fall back to NATIVE

A KV consumer may select `PreprocessType.PROLOG_V3`, prepare its fused weights, and dispose the native projection weights during initialization. In `AscendSFAImpl.forward`, an attention state other than `DecodeOnly` or `SpecDecoding` nevertheless changes the local `fused_type` back to `NATIVE`.

This is reachable for multi-token verification/chunked-prefill and prefix-cache-hit states. The NATIVE branch subsequently calls `fused_qkv_a_proj`, even though the weights required by that branch have already been released.

Expected behavior: once a KV consumer has selected PROLOG_V3 and disposed native weights, supported runtime attention states must stay on PROLOG_V3. The legacy attention-state and token-count fallback should apply only to MLAPO.

#### 2. Compiled MoE can freeze the wrong final-reduction decision

`MoERunner.forward()` evaluates `_maybe_reduce_final_output` outside the existing fused MoE custom-op boundary. The result depends on the live MoE communication method:

  * `ALLGATHER` without sequence parallelism requires the outer TP all-reduce.
  * `MC2` and `ALLTOALL` already reduce the routed output.

A graph traced/profiled with one method can be replayed when another method is selected for the runtime batch. The Python guard is not retraced, so the graph may double-reduce the output or omit a required reduction, causing severe accuracy loss.

Expected behavior: the communication-dependent reduction decision must remain runtime-visible instead of being frozen by the first trace.

### Reproduction coverage

The failures are covered by focused tests using:

  * SFA states `DecodeOnly`, `ChunkedPrefill`, and `PrefillCacheHit`, with PROLOG_V3 native projection access made fatal after simulated weight disposal.
  * A single `make_fx` MoE graph replayed while switching the live communication method across `ALLGATHER`, `MC2`, and `ALLTOALL`.
  * DSpark profile shapes with `max_num_batched_tokens` 256/1024, 64 requests, 7 speculative tokens, and both anchor-sampling layouts.

### Reference implementation

Draft PR #16482 is provided for reference only. It records the implementation used to validate the identified root causes and regression tests; it is not presented as the final merge proposal.

In particular, its MoE portion overlaps with #16455, #16459, and #16476, so maintainers may choose one of those approaches instead. The SFA and DSpark changes can also be reviewed or split independently.

The reference draft keeps PROLOG_V3 on its prepared path, puts the complete MoE runner call behind an opaque runtime boundary, grows the DSpark profile ID buffer, and explicitly constructs the draft model under the eager context.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As a result, we suspect that there may be an anomaly in the underlying communication of vllm-ascend, which could lead to occasional accuracy issues.
    
    `

After initial localization, we observed that there are occasional, significant fluctuations (0.5~1) in the logits after each first token inference. This fluctuation is clearly abnormal, prompting us to conduct further checks on the operator behavior.

Through deeper analysis, we found that the expert selection of the fused operator moe_gate_topk exhibits significant fluctuations. The root cause lies in the abnormal output of the upstream allreduce communication operator. Therefore, we conducted a series of experiments.

We discovered:

  1. After replacing the moe_gate_topk with small operations, the probability of model accuracy degradation was significantly reduced.
  2. After enabling deterministic computation（export HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=true）, the model's accuracy was tested with over 3000 badcase test cases and no issues were reproduced (previously 5%).

As a result, we suspect that there may be an anomaly in the underlying communication of vllm-ascend, which could lead to occasional accuracy issues.

Since deterministic computation may cause noticeable performance degradation, we will avoid using this method to mitigate accuracy issues whenever possible. In the next step, we will disable the hierarchical communication feature (HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1) for further verification and in-depth analysis of the communication behavior.

citeturn116search7 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3 weeks ago; Crawled: 3 weeks ago; This report does not claim an observed end-to-end accuracy regression. ... In a vllm-ascend checkout containing the referenced upstream commit, inspect the kernel constants:
    
    git show bc975f29e01ad45a1016176b67f29421e96f888c:csrc/mla_preprocess/op_kernel/mla_preprocess_mix_bf16_qdown.hpp \
The links below use fixed commits.

### Describe the bug

MLAPO hardcodes `1e-6` for both Q and KV RMSNorm instead of using the model's configured epsilon. The deployed GLM-5.2 W8A8 checkpoint specifies `rms_norm_eps=1e-5`.

The native/model path constructs the Q and KV normalization layers using `config.rms_norm_eps`, whereas the fused MLAPO kernel uses a different constant. This changes the normalization formula when the configured epsilon is not `1e-6`.

Confirmed: a model-parameter mismatch in the implementation. Not yet measured: its effect on full-model generation accuracy or benchmark scores. This report does not claim an observed end-to-end accuracy regression.

### 1. Model configuration evidence

The following excerpt was read directly from the deployed checkpoint's `config.json`:
    
    {
      "rms_norm_eps": 1e-5,
      "q_lora_rank": 2048,
      "kv_lora_rank": 512,
      "qk_nope_head_dim": 192,
      "qk_rope_head_dim": 64,
      "dtype": "bfloat16"
    }

## Model

Qwen3-32B w8a8 / QuaRot

## Issue

On `releases/v0.26.0rc`, some A2 PD disaggregation and nightly tests show a small performance regression. With pooling enabled, TPS is `2313` versus `2443` without pooling (about 5.3% lower).

The A3 single-machine token-in/token-out case also fails to start in graph mode because of a `batch_invariant_ops` error.

This issue will be tracked in the follow-up sunset plan.
